title: Crop Problem Guides: Pests, Diseases and Weeds of Philippine Farms
metaTitle: Crop Problems in the Philippines: Free Field Guides
metaDescription: Free guides to crop problems in the Philippines: rice and corn pests, plant diseases and weeds. Learn the signs, the causes and what to do about each one.
excerpt: The anee.io crop problem guides are free field guides to the crop problems Filipino farmers meet most: the pests, diseases and weeds of palay, mais, vegetables and fruit. Each guide shows how to spot the problem, why it comes and what to do about it, with the local names farmers use. You do not need an account to read them.

blocks.text: What the crop problem guides cover

Every guide follows the same order, so you know where to look. It opens with a photo and what the problem is. Then come the signs in the field, why it builds up and how to manage it, with cultural control first and chemicals last. Each one ends with the questions farmers ask and the sources behind it, from PhilRice, IRRI, the DA and the product labels.

On the [crop problems page](/problems), filter by rice pests, corn pests, crop pests, rice diseases, crop diseases or weeds.

items: [Brown planthopper](/problems/brown-planthopper): the sap sucker behind hopperburn, and why an early spray can make it worse

[Rice leaffolder](/problems/rice-leaffolder): the mambibilot that folds leaves, and when its damage really matters
[Rice insects](/problems/rice-insects): the main pests by crop stage, and the spiders and wasps that eat them for free
[Fall armyworm](/problems/fall-armyworm): the caterpillar first reported in Cagayan in 2019, and how to scout for it
[Asian corn borer](/problems/asian-corn-borer): the stalk borer, with detasseling, Trichogramma and Bt corn
[Cutworm](/problems/cutworm): the night feeder that cuts corn seedlings and young vegetable stems

blocks.text: How to use the guides in the field

Start with what you see, not with a chemical. Walk the field, note the crop stage and look closely at the leaf, the stem and the base of the hill. Then match it against the guide. Many problems look alike from the road. A brown patch in palay (rice still in the husk) may be hopperburn, bugburn or a disease, and each needs a different answer. Our [rice insects](/problems/rice-insects) guide shows how to tell an insect from a disease before you spray.

items.title: Look and take a photo
items.text: Take a sharp photo in daylight of the damage and, if you can, of the insect itself.

items.title: Match it to a guide
items.text: Compare the signs, the crop stage and the recent weather with what the guide describes.

items.title: Check if it pays to act
items.text: Several guides give counts or damage levels before a spray pays off. Below that, natural enemies often do the job for you.

items.title: Follow the label
items.text: If you must spray, use a product registered for that crop and pest, and follow its label. Our page on the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority) explains the registration.

blocks.text: Not sure? Ask with a photo

When you cannot tell, a plan with Anee lets you send the photo to [Anee, the AI technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician) in anee.io. She looks at the picture, weighs it against your crop and its stage, and tells you what she sees and what to check next. Treat her reading as a first opinion, and call your municipal agriculturist for a serious outbreak.
From the guide to your board

The guides tell you what to watch for, and anee.io helps you watch at the right time. [Growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) lists what to look for at each lot's stage. [Anee's tip of the day](/features/farm-tip-of-the-day) may name the pest of the week, like the rice black bug at tillering. Put each scouting walk or spray on [today on the board](/features/daily-farm-tasks) so it gets a date and a tick.

Halfway through the season, [Analyze So Far](/features/analyze-so-far) weighs the risks ahead for each lot. When one of those risks is a pest or a disease, the matching guide is one tap away.

blocks.title: Never spray on a guess
blocks.text: A wrong spray costs money and kills the spiders and wasps that keep pests down. Confirm the problem first, use only FPA registered products and follow the label for the rate, the timing and your safety.

blocks.title: Catch crop problems at the right stage
blocks.text: Read the guides free, any time. Sign up free to see each lot's stage, what to watch for and a daily tip on your phone.

items.a: Yes. Anyone can read them on the web, with or without an anee.io account.

items.q: Which crops do the guides cover?
items.a: Mostly palay and corn, plus mango, sili, onion, banana, tomato and other vegetables where a pest or disease hits them.

items.q: Do the guides give spray rates?
items.a: They name the active ingredients and their groups, then point you to the product label for the rate. Always follow the label and the FPA registration.

items.q: How do I tell an insect problem from a disease?
items.a: Look for the insect itself, its eggs or its droppings, and check where the damage starts. The rice insects guide walks you through it.

items.q: Where do the facts come from?
items.a: From PhilRice, IRRI, the DA and its regional offices, universities and the makers' own label pages. Each guide lists its sources at the end.
